commits.edited_message:
pcre2posix: do not truncate the subject length to int in regexec (#1022)

REG_STARTEND subjects are not NUL-terminated, so match them from a
temporary holding exactly the widened size_t span.

Co-authored-by: Manohar Paturi <manoharpaturi@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

posix: validate REG_STARTEND offsets and NULL pointer arguments (#1009)

After the offsets are checked, copy from the end value those checks
accepted rather than from the byte before it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: abbf691 adds regexec_copy_region(), which copies the closed range [start, end] (n = end - start + 1) and calls it with end = eo - 1, so the temporary holds exactly the half-open REG_STARTEND span while pcre2_match is still given length eo - so. That commit stays in bounds. 2d3a98a does not change the helper; it passes the exclusive eo that the offset checks just accepted (the same end the match length is computed from) instead of eo - 1. Each diff follows one convention — inclusive last byte versus the validated exclusive end — and neither diff overruns under the convention it uses. The one-byte memcpy past rm_eo appears only when the inclusive copier is combined with the exclusive argument. The first edited commit alone still passes eo - 1; the second hunk has no call to retarget until that helper exists. Repair means reconciling the two conventions, which is not visible as an out-of-bounds access inside either diff on its own.
